Case Name: PostgreSQL backend stores and serves AgentCards
Precondition:
1. registry-center image <IMAGE_TAG> is deployed and a PostgreSQL 14+ instance is reachable from the service
2. etc/conf/db/postgresql.json sets host/port/database/user and names its credential with password_env=REGISTRY_DB_SECRET; REGISTRY_DB_SECRET is injected into the service environment
3. etc/conf/persistence.conf sets persistence.mode=postgresql
4. A signed AgentCard sample (name test-pg-agent, provider.organization test-org) is stored at <CARD_FILE>
Steps:
1. Start registry-center and poll GET /health until it returns 200 (see result 1)
2. POST /rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards with body {"agentCards":[<card from <CARD_FILE>>]} (see result 2)
3. GET /rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards?name=test-pg-agent&organization=test-org (see result 3)
4. Run SELECT name, organization, status FROM agent_card WHERE name='test-pg-agent' against the configured database (see result 4)
5. Cleanup: DELETE /rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards/test-org/test-pg-agent (see result 5)
Expected Result:
1. GET /health returns 200 with {"status":"ok"} and the startup log reports PostgreSQL storage initialized (no fallback to file storage)
2. Returns 201 and results[0] carries name=test-pg-agent, organization=test-org, status=published, registrySigned=true
3. Returns 200, agentCards holds exactly one card whose name and provider.organization match the payload
4. Exactly one row exists with status 'published' in the configured database and data/agentcard.json does not contain the card
5. Returns 200 with name, organization and deleted=true; the SELECT in step 4 returns 0 rows afterwards

Case Name: Persistence mode switch needs a restart
Precondition:
1. registry-center running locally from docker-compose.yml with persistence.mode=file and card test-switch-agent registered
2. A PostgreSQL instance is reachable from the compose network with etc/conf/db/postgresql.json ready
Steps:
1. Record the current list with GET /rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards (see result 1)
2. Change persistence.conf to persistence.mode=postgresql while the service keeps running, then GET the list and register test-switch-2 (see result 2)
3. Query the agent_card table in PostgreSQL for the pre-existing card (see result 3)
4. Restart the container and GET the list again (see result 4)
5. Cleanup: delete both cards where they exist and restore persistence.mode=file (see result 5)
Expected Result:
1. Returns 200 and the list contains test-switch-agent (file backend)
2. The running instance keeps answering from the file backend: test-switch-agent is still listed and test-switch-2 registers with 201; no online hot migration happens
3. PostgreSQL holds no row for the pre-existing test-switch-agent (the switch only affects a restarted process)
4. After the restart the list is served by PostgreSQL and contains test-switch-2 but not the file-only card
5. Deletions return 200 deleted=true and persistence.mode is back to file
Notes: design_method:State Transition;environment:docker-compose;language_profile:python;protocol_primitive:none;execution_strategy:full;issue #3 explicitly excludes online hot migration; the restart here applies a configuration change and is not failure recovery (no DFR scenario);verification source: docs/database-configuration.md#L27-L31 (restart required, fixed connection and dialect)

3. GET /rest/v1/registry-center/agents/health?status=offline (see result 3)
4. GET /rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards?name=hb-agent-2 (see result 4)
5. Cleanup: DELETE the card and re-read agents/health (see result 5)
Expected Result:
1. The heartbeat returns 200 with health_status=healthy

5. DELETE returns 200 and agents/health no longer contains the agent

Case Name: Registration change is delivered to a subscriber
Precondition:
1. broadcast.enabled=true, broadcast.allow.http.callbacks=true, broadcast.callback.allowlist=<RECEIVER_HOST>
2. An HTTP receiver at http://<RECEIVER_HOST>:<PORT>/hook records request bodies and X-Registry-* headers
3. broadcast timing keeps the shipped defaults (broadcast.debounce.window=2.0)
Steps:
1. POST /rest/v1/registry-center/subscriptions with callback_url http://<RECEIVER_HOST>:<PORT>/hook, event_types ["AGENT_REGISTERED"], filters.organizations ["<org>"] and secret <SECRET> (see result 1)
2. POST /rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards with card <org>/bc-agent-1 (see result 2)
3. Wait for the receiver to record a delivery using the framework retry helper (see result 3)
4. GET /rest/v1/registry-center/changes?since=0 (see result 4)
5. Cleanup: DELETE the subscription and the card, then confirm no further delivery arrives (see result 5)
Expected Result:
1. Returns 201 with subscription_id matching sub_<20 hex chars>, the callback_url and event_types echoed, and the secret is never echoed in the response body
2. Returns 201 with results[0].status=published
3. The receiver recorded one POST whose body holds subscription_id and events[] with event_type AGENT_REGISTERED and data.name=bc-agent-1, plus X-Registry-Event-Id, X-Registry-Timestamp headers and X-Registry-Signature whose value equals the HMAC computed over timestamp + body with <SECRET>
4. Returns 200; changes contains the AGENT_REGISTERED event for bc-agent-1 with a registry_version and next_since not below it
5. Both deletions return 200 and no further delivery is recorded afterwards
Notes: design_method:Scenario Method;environment:with-workload-cluster;language_profile:python;protocol_primitive:none;execution_strategy:smoke;callback allowlist and HTTP switch are enforced at subscription time;verification source: agent_registry/broadcast/dispatcher.py#L402-L424 (payload, HMAC headers) and agent_registry/server.py#L1855-L1901, L1945-L1967
